## Web App Feasibility for DopaFry (OpalClone)

**Short answer: ~70% of features port cleanly, ~30% need workarounds or get degraded.**

### What ports easily (core value prop intact)
- Dopamine debt tracking & meter
- Task initiation ("Start" button + timer)
- Impulse logging & resistance tracking
- Dopamine Coin currency system
- Coach system (5 personalities, RSD-safe messaging)
- Recovery hub (breathing, movement, grounding)
- Daily check-ins, streaks, achievements
- Task transitions
- All 13 data models → PostgreSQL

### What gets degraded or lost
| iOS Feature | Web Reality |
|---|---|
| **App blocking** (Family Controls) | Need a **browser extension** for site blocking only — can't block native apps |
| **Passive device monitoring** | Can only track browser usage, not phone pickups or native app opens |
| **Live Activities / Dynamic Island** | Web push notifications (less reliable) |
| **HealthKit** | Google Fit / Fitbit APIs (different ecosystem) |
| **Haptic feedback** | Vibration API (limited support) |
| **Motion detection** (phone pickups) | No equivalent |
| **Background audio** (ambient sounds) | Works but stops if tab is backgrounded |

### Recommended approach
**Web app + browser extension combo:**
- **Next.js/React web app** — all core features, PWA for offline
- **Chrome/Firefox extension** — site blocking + usage tracking
- **Backend** (Node or Python) — debt calculation, auth, notifications

### Effort estimate
- **MVP (core features):** ~2-3 months
- **Full parity (minus native-only stuff):** ~4-5 months
- **Browser extension add-on:** +2-3 weeks

### Biggest wins of going web
- No App Store review / entitlement approval delays (Screen Time API is currently blocked waiting on Apple)
- Cross-platform immediately (Windows, Mac, Linux, Chromebook)
- Easier onboarding (no install friction)
- Can iterate faster

### Biggest risks
- Losing the "always-on" passive monitoring that makes the iOS version powerful
- Hyperfocus detection becomes heuristic (time-on-page) instead of native
- Web push notifications are less reliable than iOS notifications

**Bottom line:** The core ADHD value — dopamine debt tracking, task initiation rewards, impulse resistance, coaching — translates fully to web. The hardware/OS-level features (app blocking, device monitoring) are the main casualties. A browser extension recovers some of that for desktop users.

## AfriCal Web Conversion: Very Feasible

**Short answer: This is a much easier conversion than OpalClone. ~90% of features port cleanly to web.**

### Why it's easy

- **No heavy native dependencies** — no Screen Time API, no Family Controls, no device monitoring
- **Already uses REST APIs** — OpenAI Vision + OpenFoodFacts work identically from a browser
- **Simple data models** — only 3 core models (MealEntry, WeightEntry, MealTemplate) + UserDefaults
- **Clean architecture** — logic is well-separated from UI
- **54 Swift files total** — relatively small codebase

### Feature-by-feature breakdown

| Feature | Web Difficulty | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Meal logging (manual) | **Easy** | Standard form |
| Photo food recognition (OpenAI Vision) | **Easy** | Same API, just use file upload |
| Barcode scanning | **Easy-Medium** | ZXing.js works in browser via camera |
| Voice logging | **Easy-Medium** | Web Speech API is solid |
| Nutrition tracking + macro rings | **Easy** | SVG/Canvas, tons of chart libs |
| Weight tracking + trends | **Easy** | Recharts / Chart.js |
| Fasting timer | **Easy** | JavaScript timer |
| Streak & achievements | **Easy** | Pure logic, no native deps |
| Progress photos | **Easy** | Upload to cloud storage (S3/Cloudinary) |
| CSV export | **Easy** | Trivial in JS |
| Meal templates | **Easy** | CRUD operations |
| Notifications/reminders | **Medium** | Web Push API + service worker |
| HealthKit (steps/calories) | **Hard** | No web equivalent — would need Google Fit API, Fitbit API, or manual entry |
| Haptic feedback | **N/A** | Skip for web |
| Confetti/particle animations | **Easy** | Framer Motion, canvas-confetti, etc. |

### What you'd need

**Recommended stack:**
- **Next.js + TypeScript** — frontend
- **Tailwind CSS** — styling (African-inspired palette ports directly)
- **Supabase or Firebase** — auth + database + image storage
- **Stripe** — subscriptions (replaces StoreKit)
- **Recharts or Chart.js** — analytics charts

### Effort estimate

- **Core MVP (meal logging + nutrition tracking + analytics):** ~4-6 weeks
- **Full feature parity (minus HealthKit):** ~10-12 weeks
- **Only real feature loss:** HealthKit step/calorie data

### Compared to OpalClone

AfriCal is **significantly easier** to convert:
- OpalClone depends on iOS-only APIs (Screen Time, Family Controls, Device Activity) that are core to its value
- AfriCal's core value (food logging + AI recognition + nutrition tracking) is **platform-agnostic**
- AfriCal is ~54 files vs OpalClone's ~125 files

**Verdict: Go for it.** This is a clean, straightforward conversion. The hardest part is just building the UI — all the business logic and APIs translate directly.
